skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray showing complete opacification of one hemithorax with ipsilateral mediastinal shift to distinguish between lung agenesis, aplasia, and hypoplasia.
steps: Confirm complete opacification of the affected hemithorax and verify significant mediastinal shift toward the opaque side (indicating volume loss rather than mass effect).
Inspect the contralateral lung for compensatory hyperinflation and herniation across the midline into the opaque hemithorax.

Differentiate based on bronchial anatomy: Agenesis implies total absence of lung and bronchus; Aplasia implies absent lung parenchyma but presence of a rudimentary blind-ending bronchus; Hypoplasia implies presence of a small, aerated lung with reduced volume.
